newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel to be at Bundesbank council meeting - sources.
newsitem.headline: Waigel to be at Bundesbank council meeting - sources.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel will attend today's meeting of the Bundesbank council, coalition sources said on Thursday.
German media reports say the government is weighing plans to revalue the Bundesbank's reserves to boost the budget, but a Finance Ministry spokeswoman denied earlier that gold sales were planned.
Bundesbank officials said Waigel was not present as the meeting began, but declined to comment on whether he would arrive later.
The Berliner Zeitung newspaper reported Waigel is seeking a higher valuation of Bundesbank assets in a bid to raise further cash for Bonn's budget coffers.

In a release issued ahead of publication in Friday's edition, the newspaper reported that the Bonn government was urging Bonn to put a higher book value on its dollar, foreign currency and gold assets to boost the central bank's profits.
The Bundesbank currently books its assets at their all-time lowest price, a method which is normal under German book-keeping regulations.
